suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is read without optional chaining, and mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty. WHY: any Google Meet booking where neither the organizer nor the event type has a destination calendar throws a TypeError, and booking creation fails. The old code used `?.`. HOW: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: references for non-calendar results (video) now get `credentialId: undefined`, where they used to get result.credentialId. WHY: handleCancelBooking only deletes video meetings when the video reference has a credentialId, so Zoom/Daily meetings are no longer deleted on cancel. HOW: keep result.credentialId for every result type.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the fallback only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, but it then searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, so it never matches a real calendar. WHY: the calendar id becomes undefined, which drops the old fallback to destinationCalendar.externalId and sends updates for legacy references to the wrong calendar or makes them fail. HOW: fall back to the first destination calendar's externalId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the deleteEvent fallback searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always returns undefined. WHY: for references without externalCalendarId, the destination calendar fallback is lost and the delete falls back to the default calendar. If the event lives in a different calendar, it is left behind. HOW: use `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, so `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing. WHY: in collective events where the first host has no destination calendar, the other hosts' calendars are silently dropped, which is the case this PR is supposed to fix. HOW: default to `[]` instead of null.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: createEvent always uses destinationCalendar[0].externalId. createAllCalendarEvents now calls it once per host credential, so every host's Office365 credential gets the first host's calendar id. WHY: a second collective host using Office365 posts to `/me/calendars/<host1-calendar-id>/events`, which does not exist in their account, so their event creation fails. HOW: pick the destination entry whose credentialId matches this credential, as GoogleCalendarService does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the recurring-series branch, which deletes the events of all updatedBookings for every user calendar credential, now sits inside the per-reference loop. WHY: with multiple calendar references, the same recurring events get one delete call per reference, which causes duplicate API calls and 404/410 errors. HOW: move the recurring deletion out of the reference loop so it runs once.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the slug condition was flipped from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`. WHY: with billing enabled, the slug is set right away and also stored as requestedSlug, and with billing disabled, organizations are created with no slug. HOW: restore the negation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the catch block turns the plain Error thrown for an empty or invalid dynamicUserList into a generic 500 'Unable to load users'. WHY: a client input error comes back as a server error with its message hidden. HOW: throw `new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, ... })` directly for the validation failure.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses `&&` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, and isTeamAdmin already matches ADMIN or OWNER roles, so the check passes only for OWNERs. WHY: Team ADMINs who are not the organizer or an attendee get FORBIDDEN, even though the variable name says admins should be allowed. HOW: Use `||`, or just call isTeamAdmin, which already covers owners.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails gets the raw `guests` input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`. WHY: An already-existing attendee who appears in the submitted list is treated as a new guest and gets a 'new booking scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notice. HOW: Pass `uniqueGuests`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: EventManager is built from the caller's (ctx.user) credentials, but updateCalendarAttendees updates the booking references that live in the organizer's calendar. WHY: When an attendee or team owner adds guests, the calendar update runs with credentials that don't own those events, so the organizer's calendar event never gets the new attendees, or the update throws. HOW: Build EventManager from booking.user and that user's credentials, as other booking handlers do.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: updateCalendarAttendees runs after attendees are already saved to the database, and it is not wrapped in error handling. WHY: If the calendar provider call fails, the client gets an error but the guests stay saved without emails, and a retry is rejected with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. HOW: Wrap the calendar update in try/catch and log the error so emails still go out and the mutation reports success.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Blacklist entries are lowercased, but each guest email is compared with its original casing. WHY: Submitting a blacklisted address with any uppercase letter (e.g. `Bad@x.com`) gets past BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and the address is added and emailed. HOW: Lowercase the guest before comparing it to the blacklist and to existing attendees.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The server schema accepts duplicate emails in `guests`, and the handler only removes guests that are already attendees, not repeats within the input. WHY: A direct API call with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows via createMany, because the uniqueness check exists only on the client. HOW: Add a refine that rejects duplicates (or dedupe with a Set in the handler).

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `guests` has no maximum length, and any booking attendee is allowed to call the mutation. WHY: An authenticated attendee can submit thousands of arbitrary addresses in one request, and each one gets a calendar-invite email sent in the organizer's name, which turns this endpoint into a spam relay. HOW: Cap the array size (e.g. `.max(10)`), on top of rate limiting.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParse result object, and that object is written directly as credential.key. WHY: the DB key becomes {success, data}, so googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) at line 75 throws for every later request and the Google credential becomes unusable after the first refresh. HOW: store the parsed data.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: when credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this code reads res?.data as if it were a Gaxios response. WHY: token is undefined, so token.access_token throws a TypeError and Google tokens can never be refreshed in sync mode. HOW: in the sync branch, parse the Response JSON before using it, or make refreshOAuthTokens return the same shape that each caller expects.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: credentialId is passed where refreshOAuthTokens expects the credential's userId. WHY: the sync endpoint receives a credential id as calcomUserId, so it returns tokens for the wrong user or for none. HOW: pass the credential's userId instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: in sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this code reads tokenInfo.data.error as if it were an axios response. WHY: tokenInfo.data is undefined, so the property access throws and the token refresh always fails when sync is enabled. HOW: await the Response's json() in the sync branch and use that value as the token data.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: both computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to the literal property name '[object Object]', so the schema only declares access_token plus a field named '[object Object]'. WHY: zod strips every other field (expires_in, expiry_date, scope, token_type), so sync-mode refreshes lose expiry information and callers such as Zoom (expires_in) and office365 get NaN or missing values. HOW: use z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough(), with explicit optional expiry fields if needed.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: when the parsed response has no refresh_token, the code writes the literal string "refresh_token" into it. WHY: office365calendar spreads tokenResponse.data over the stored credentials (line 264), so a provider response without refresh_token (always the case with the stripping minimum schema) replaces the real stored refresh token with the string 'refresh_token', and the next refresh fails. HOW: remove the placeholder assignment so callers keep their existing refresh_token.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the new code calls prisma.credential.update, but the file never imports prisma. Imports at lines 1-20 have no @calcom/prisma. WHY: this causes a TypeScript compile error or a ReferenceError at runtime, which rejects getClient so every Salesforce operation fails. HOW: add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: success is detected by comparing response.statusText to "OK". WHY: statusText is empty over HTTP/2 and in many fetch implementations, so successful refreshes throw a 400 and the Salesforce client can never be created. HOW: check response.ok instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the token is refreshed and saved, but jsforce.Connection is still built with the old credentialKey.access_token and instance_url. WHY: the refresh result is discarded for the current connection, so requests use the stale or expired token. HOW: pass accessTokenParsed.data.access_token and accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url to the Connection.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: getClient runs on every SalesforceCalendarService construction and always makes a token refresh HTTP call plus a credential DB write, without checking whether the token is expired. WHY: this adds an external round-trip and a DB write to every booking or calendar operation, and frequent refreshes can hit Salesforce rate limits. HOW: refresh only when the token is invalid or expired, or rely on jsforce's built-in refresh handling.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: appStoreMetadata is indexed by app.slug, but the map is keyed by app directory name (see _appRegistry.ts:17, which uses app.dirName). WHY: for apps whose slug differs from their dirName (e.g. google-calendar vs googlecalendar), the lookup returns undefined and the webhook always responds 404, so those credentials cannot be synced. HOW: select dirName from prisma.app and index appStoreMetadata by it.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the webhook secret is checked with a plain !== string comparison. WHY: this endpoint can overwrite any user's third-party credentials, and a non-constant-time comparison exposes the secret to timing analysis. HOW: compare using crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers after confirming the header is a string.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: when state.teamId is present, the code only checks that the user is an accepted team member before creating a team credential, and throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam runs only on the path where teamId is falsy, so it is effectively a no-op. WHY: any non-admin team member can install OAuth apps on behalf of the team through a crafted state parameter. HOW: call throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({ teamId: state.teamId, userId }) inside the teamId branch before prisma.credential.create.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: in sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the result is used directly as a HubspotToken. WHY: expiresIn and accessToken are undefined on a Response, so expiryDate becomes NaN, a Response object is persisted as the credential key, and setAccessToken(undefined) is called. HOW: parse the Response JSON in the sync branch before treating it as a token.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `retryCount > 1` branch of the deleteMany OR has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so the SMS cron deletes any WorkflowReminder (email or WhatsApp) whose retryCount is above 1. WHY: Once another cron starts incrementing retryCount, this job will silently delete reminders for other methods. HOW: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retryCount condition.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new retryCount increment sits inside `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)`, so a reminder with a missing phone number or an empty message never increments its counter. WHY: These reminders can never succeed, but they are still re-fetched and re-processed on every cron run until scheduledDate passes, which is the behavior the PR is meant to stop. HOW: Move the increment into an else branch of the outer `if` as well, or into one failure path that covers both cases.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The prisma.workflowReminder.update added in the catch block has no guard, so if it throws (for example P2025 because the reminder was deleted, or a DB error), the exception escapes the for-loop. WHY: All remaining reminders in this cron run are skipped and the handler returns an error instead of continuing. HOW: Wrap the catch-block update in its own try/catch, or use updateMany, which does not throw when no row matches.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Every failure from twilio.scheduleSMS increments retryCount, including temporary ones: an undefined return while the account is SMS-locked, a throw from checkSMSRateLimit when the monthly limit is hit, and Twilio network or 5xx errors. WHY: Two consecutive cron runs with a temporary failure permanently delete a valid reminder, so the attendee never gets the SMS even after the condition clears. HOW: Increment retryCount only for permanent errors, such as Twilio invalid-number error codes, and let temporary errors retry without counting.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: retryCount is written as `reminder.retryCount + 1` from a value read earlier, not with an atomic increment. WHY: Overlapping cron invocations processing the same reminder overwrite each other and lose increments. HOW: Use `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new backup-code branch is evaluated even when the password check was skipped. The existing guard `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` skips verifyPassword whenever totpCode is non-empty, and the backup-code branch then ignores totpCode entirely. WHY: An attacker who has a victim's email and one leaked backup code can POST credentials with `totpCode=x` and `backupCode=<code>` and log in without the password, so the backup code replaces both factors. HOW: Require that the password was verified before accepting a backup code. For example, reject when `credentials.backupCode` is set and the password check did not run, or run verifyPassword unconditionally in the backup-code branch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Spending a backup code is a non-atomic read-decrypt-modify-write of `user.backupCodes`, with no lock and no condition that the stored value is unchanged. WHY: Two concurrent login requests with the same code both read the old list, both find the code, and both succeed, so a single-use code can authenticate multiple sessions. HOW: Make the update conditional on the previously read ciphertext (`updateMany({ where: { id: user.id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes }, ... })`) and reject the login if count is 0.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: 2FA is already enabled on the server when the DisplayBackupCodes step is shown, but onEnable() and resetState() run only from the Close button; dismissing the dialog with Escape or an overlay click goes through the parent's onOpenChange, which just toggles `enableModalOpen`. WHY: After that dismissal, viewer.me is never invalidated, so the switch stays unchecked even though 2FA is on. The next time the modal opens it starts on the stale backup-codes step instead of ConfirmPassword. HOW: Wrap onOpenChange so that closing while `step === SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` calls resetState() and onEnable().

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`), but the user's input is compared exactly after stripping only dashes, with no case normalization. WHY: A user who types the code in uppercase, which the 'XXXXX-XXXXX' placeholder invites, gets IncorrectBackupCode and can be locked out of recovery. HOW: Normalize with `.toLowerCase()` before indexOf.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged for raw_html posts, so HTML imported from RSS (after CGI.unescapeHTML) or from remote pages is stored as `cooked` with no sanitization. WHY: <script> tags, event handlers or `javascript:` hrefs in feed or page content run in the Discourse origin wherever cooked is rendered (topic view and the embed iframe use `raw post.cooked`), which is stored XSS. HOW: run the raw HTML through the same whitelist sanitizer the normal pipeline uses (e.g. PrettyText's sanitize step) before returning it.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `url` is interpolated into `#{url}` without HTML escaping, and it comes from the user-supplied embed_url parameter (TopicRetriever only checks the host). WHY: a URL like `http://host/'onmouseover='alert(1)` is a valid URI and breaks out of the attribute, injecting an event handler into the imported post. HOW: escape the URL with ERB::Util.html_escape in both the attribute and the link text.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The throttle key is the full embed URL, and anonymous requests to /embed/best (whose Referer can be forged by non-browser clients) enqueue retrieve jobs that create topics. WHY: an attacker can vary the query string or path on the embeddable host (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, ...) to get past the throttle and make the server create an unlimited number of topics as embed_by_username. HOW: throttle per client or globally rather than per URL, and normalize the URL (or drop the query string) before using it as the throttle key and embed key.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: For every embed URL that is not yet imported, perform_retrieve runs Jobs::PollFeed synchronously, which downloads the whole feed and runs TopicEmbed.import for every item. WHY: every retrieval for an unknown URL (which an anonymous caller can trigger repeatedly with distinct URLs) costs a full feed fetch with no timeout plus N import/SHA comparisons, so worker time grows with feed size × request rate. HOW: rely on the hourly scheduled poll, or cache the last poll time in Redis and skip the inline poll if one ran recently.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/a.png`, and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes. WHY: external links and images become `http://host/cdn.example.com/a.png`, which breaks them in every imported post. HOW: skip values that start with `//` (and do the same for img src).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `i.content.scrub` assumes every feed item has a <content> element, but standard RSS 2.0 items often only have <description>, in which case SimpleRSS returns nil for content. WHY: the NoMethodError on nil aborts the whole poll (retry: false) and also aborts the inline poll inside TopicRetriever, so no items are imported. HOW: fall back to description and skip items that have no body.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `post = embed.post` can be nil when the imported post has been deleted (soft-deleted posts are excluded by the default scope), and it is passed straight to PostRevisor. WHY: when the feed content changes, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError, which aborts the feed poll for every remaining item. HOW: return early (or recreate the post) when embed.post is nil.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `<%- end if %>` leaves a dangling `if` modifier, so the next compiled template expression (the logo output) becomes the condition of the whole if/else block. WHY: the logo is written to the buffer before the header button, so the header renders in the wrong order. HOW: use a plain `<%- end %>`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `execute(...)[0]['id']` (and `[0]['value']` on line 15) assumes the query returns a row. On sites where embed_category is unset or does not match a category name, or where uncategorized_category_id is not stored in site_settings, it returns none. WHY: `[0]` is nil, so the migration raises NoMethodError and the deploy fails. HOW: Check the result's ntuples before indexing and fall back to a default.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Legacy embeddable_hosts values (often 'http://host', with paths or trailing \r) are inserted raw, skipping the model's scheme/path stripping. WHY: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares the column against the bare uri.host, so migrated entries like 'http://discourse.org' never match, and embedding stops working for existing sites after upgrade. HOW: Before inserting, strip whitespace, the scheme and any path from each value.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Host values from site_settings are interpolated directly into an INSERT statement as '#{h}'. WHY: A value containing a single quote breaks the migration or injects arbitrary SQL that runs with migration privileges. HOW: Quote the value with connection.quote(h).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The query lowercases the column (`lower(host)`) but compares it to uri.host without downcasing it. WHY: A referer or embed URL with uppercase characters (e.g. 'http://EvilTrout.com/x') fails the check, and embedding is wrongly rejected. HOW: Downcase the argument.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The validation regex accepts a port and before_validation keeps it in the stored host ('example.com:8080'), but record_for_host compares against uri.host, which never includes the port. WHY: Hosts saved with a port pass validation and can never match a referer, so embedding from them always fails. HOW: Either compare host plus port (when it is not the default port), or strip the port before saving.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: before_validation calls `self.host.sub!` with no nil guard. WHY: A create/update request without a host param (or EmbeddableHost.new without a host) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. HOW: Return early when host is nil.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: destroy (and update) use `where(id:).first`, which returns nil for an unknown id, and then call methods on it. WHY: Deleting or updating a host that does not exist (or was already deleted) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404. HOW: Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` so ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound returns a 404.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new `_ids` branch runs for every key ending in `_ids` on every hydrated model. It always deletes the original key and replaces it with the result of mapping _lookupSubType, which returns undefined when the root has no matching collection; a null value crashes on `.map`. WHY: Existing REST models with plain id-array attributes (e.g. `group_ids`) lose that data or throw while hydrating, a regression outside the embedding feature. HOW: Only replace the key when the value is an array and the pluralized collection exists in root.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the 5-argument `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, because Ruby has no overloading. WHY: `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14) still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, which now raises ArgumentError (5 for 3..4), so emoji resizing breaks. HOW: Merge them into one method that accepts both forms, e.g. `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions_or_width, max_height=nil, opts={})`, or give the new variant a different name.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: For GIFs with allow_animated_thumbnails enabled, "80%" is passed to downsize_instructions_animated, which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`; gifsicle expects WxH there, not a percentage. WHY: gifsicle fails, convert_with returns false, the file never shrinks, and all 5 attempts are wasted before the oversized GIF is rejected anyway. HOW: For animated GIFs, compute explicit pixel dimensions (80% of the current width and height) instead of passing a percentage.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: tempfile.path is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize, and convert_with runs it in a shell through backticks without escaping. For API URL uploads, that path contains the request-controlled `type` param (`discourse-upload-#{type}`). WHY: A `type` containing shell metacharacters such as `$(...)` or `;` runs arbitrary commands on the server when the oversized image is downsized. HOW: Restrict `type` to a whitelist (or Shellwords-escape every argument in convert_with) before the path reaches the shell.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Any image up to 10MB is now run through ImageMagick `convert` up to 5 times in the upload path, with no limit on pixel dimensions. WHY: A small, highly compressed image with huge pixel dimensions (a decompression bomb) makes each convert run allocate gigabytes and burn CPU, which ties up web/defer workers. HOW: Check pixel dimensions (e.g. FastImage.size) before downsizing and reject images above a sane limit.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The client-side size check now uses a hardcoded 10MB for every upload type, attachments included, instead of `max_<type>_size_kb`. WHY: Sites with max_attachment_size_kb above 10MB now see larger attachments rejected in the browser, and the error message reports the wrong limit for attachments. HOW: Keep the hardcoded 10MB only for images and keep using the site setting for other types.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `group.users.delete(user_id)` on a has_many :through removes the GroupUser row with delete_all semantics, so GroupUser callbacks (the `counter_cache: "user_count"` decrement) do not run, and the user's primary_group_id is not cleared. WHY: groups.user_count stays inflated after removals, so the admin list shows the wrong count. Removed users also keep this group as their primary group (title/flair) even though they are no longer members. HOW: destroy the join record and clear primary_group_id, as destroy_deletions does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: add_members calls group.add(user) (users.push) for every username without checking whether the user is already a member. WHY: group_users has a UNIQUE (group_id,user_id) index, so adding an existing member raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique and returns a 500, while users earlier in the list stay inserted (partial update). HOW: skip users who are already members.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which counts one page too many whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (for example 50 users with limit 50 gives 2 pages). WHY: showingLast stays false on the real last page, so 'next' moves offset to user_count and loads an empty member page labeled 2/2. HOW: use Math.ceil.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the public members endpoint takes limit straight from params with no upper bound or positivity check. WHY: any visitor can request limit=1000000 and force serialization of every member of large groups, including automatic trust-level groups. A negative limit produces a PostgreSQL error (500). HOW: clamp limit to a sane range.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The fallback locales are only loaded by FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!, and only ApplicationController calls it; I18n.translate loads just config.locale. WHY: Code that switches locale outside the controller (PostAlerter's I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale), Jobs::Base, PostDestroyer, JsLocaleHelper) falls back to :en or the site locale even when that locale was never loaded, so it returns 'translation missing' instead of the fallback text. HOW: Load the whole fallback chain where translation happens, e.g. in I18n.translate call `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` (or load each locale from `fallbacks[config.locale]`) instead of loading only config.locale.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The fallback chain now depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the translate LRU cache key is still only key+locale+backend id. WHY: A result computed before a fallback locale was loaded ('translation missing'), or before an admin changed default_locale, stays frozen in the cache and keeps being served. HOW: Add the fallback chain to the cache key, e.g. include `SiteSetting.default_locale` in `k`, or clear `@cache` when default_locale changes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an int64 deviceLimit, but pkg/server/wire.go:374-375 still registers it as a provider and binds anonstore.AnonStore to it. WHY: Wire has no provider for int64, so DI generation fails and the server won't build. The store is also no longer injected anywhere. HOW: Remove anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore and its wire.Bind from wire.go, or have the provider take *setting.Cfg and read AnonymousDeviceLimit from it.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: TagDevice now returns ErrDeviceLimitReached to block authentication, but tagDeviceUI writes the device's localCache key before CreateOrUpdateDevice runs and leaves it there when the call fails. WHY: Only the first request from a device over the limit is rejected; for the next 29 minutes the cache hit returns nil and the request is authenticated anonymously, so the limit is effectively not enforced. HOW: In tagDeviceUI, set the cache entry only after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, or delete it when the call fails.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Authenticate enforces the device limit only through TagDevice, and TagDevice returns nil when the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header is empty (impl.go:119-122). WHY: Any client that leaves out the header, or sends a fresh random ID each time, gets an anonymous identity no matter what device_limit is set to. HOW: When a device limit is configured, reject anonymous authentication for requests without a device ID.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: updateDevice treats RowsAffected()==0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached, but MySQL by default reports changed rows, not matched rows. WHY: When the limit is reached, an already-registered device whose client_ip, user_agent and second-precision updated_at are unchanged (for example, concurrent requests across instances) gets 0 rows and is wrongly denied. HOW: Check that the device exists with a SELECT on device_id within the window instead of relying on RowsAffected.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts devices and then inserts without a transaction, lock or constraint. WHY: Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < deviceLimit before any of them inserts, so the configured limit is exceeded. HOW: Run the count and insert in one transaction with appropriate locking, or do a conditional insert that checks the count in the same statement.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Device tagging used to run in a background goroutine with its own timeout and now runs inline in Authenticate. With a limit set, that means a COUNT(*) over anon_device plus an upsert for every uncached device. WHY: Anonymous authentication now waits on these DB round trips, so a slow DB or a flood of new device IDs adds latency and DB load to every such anonymous request. HOW: Keep the DB write async and enforce the limit from a cached or periodically refreshed device count.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: After taking the write lock at line 48, the code does not check entryPointAssetsCache again, so every goroutine that saw a nil cache under the RLock rebuilds it again. WHY: When the cache is empty in non-dev mode, concurrent index and frontend-settings requests queue on the mutex and each one re-reads and re-parses assets-manifest.json in turn, even after the first one has filled the cache. HOW: After Lock(), return the cached value when it is non-nil and cfg.Env != setting.Dev.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver, so every log written through FromContext goes to a throwaway instance. WHY: LoggerMiddleware now always logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so a test that injects a TestLogger and checks InfoLogs will never see the 'Plugin Request Completed' log, and logging assertions silently stop working. HOW: return the receiver so calls stay recorded on the same fake.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The async legacy write gets its timeout context from the request ctx, which the apiserver cancels as soon as the handler returns. WHY: Legacy Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection calls will often fail with context canceled, so legacy storage drifts from unified storage without any error being reported. HOW: Detach from cancellation with context.WithoutCancel(ctx) before applying the 10s timeout; Update, Delete and DeleteCollection need the same change.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Legacy.Update now gets the raw objInfo. Before this PR it got an updateWrapper holding the object that unified storage returned. WHY: Legacy recomputes the update against its own old object, using preconditions and resourceVersion meant for unified storage, so the legacy write can fail or store a different object than unified storage did. HOW: Wrap objInfo with updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res} before calling Legacy.Update.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When Storage.Create fails, the code records the failure with recordLegacyDuration. WHY: Unified storage failures show up in the legacy metric and are missing from the storage metric. HOW: Call recordStorageDuration instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When Storage.Update fails, the code records the failure with recordLegacyDuration. WHY: Unified storage update failures are attributed to legacy storage in the metrics. HOW: Call recordStorageDuration instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The goroutine that calls Legacy.DeleteCollection records its timing with recordStorageDuration. WHY: Legacy timings and errors go into the storage histogram, which skews storage metrics and hides legacy failures. HOW: Call recordLegacyDuration.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Delete passes the object name, not options.Kind, as the name label of the storage duration histogram. WHY: Each deleted object creates a new Prometheus series, so metric cardinality and memory grow without bound. HOW: Pass options.Kind.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Delete puts d.Log into the ctx instead of the log it just built with name, kind and method. WHY: Downstream logs from Storage.Delete and Legacy.Delete lose the request-specific fields, unlike the other methods in this file. HOW: Use klog.NewContext(ctx, log).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: legacyStoreMock and storageMock share one mock.Mock, so expectations set for legacy also match storage calls. WHY: For example, the Create error case only sets up the legacy mock, yet it passes because Storage.Create hits that shared expectation, so the tests can't detect a store being swapped or a legacy write being dropped. HOW: Use separate mock.Mock instances for legacy and storage.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new log line calls s.search.TotalDocs() after the watch goroutine has started (line 207). bleveBackend.TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without holding cacheMu, while that goroutine can write b.cache through getOrCreateIndex -> BuildIndex. WHY: a watch event for a namespace with no index during startup causes a concurrent map read/write, which Go treats as a fatal error and crashes the process. HOW: take b.cacheMu.RLock() inside TotalDocs, or compute the doc count before starting the watch goroutine.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When the rule is undefined (skipToken), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities still returns Duplicate as [AlwaysSupported, hasPermission(grafana create)], because loading is false and MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported. WHY: AlertRuleMenu ORs this with the ruler ability, so the Duplicate item shows for datasource/cloud rules whenever the user has the Grafana rule-create permission, even if the ruler result says it is unsupported or not allowed. HOW: Treat a missing rule as NotSupported, e.g. `const MaybeSupported = !rule || loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported;`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: canSilence can now be true from the promRule ability alone, but RuleActionsButtons.V2 only renders SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, and the list view passes only promRule. WHY: In the list view the 'Silence notifications' item shows, but clicking it sets state that never renders a drawer, so the action does nothing. HOW: Make the silence drawer render from the promRule when no ruler rule is available, or keep the item hidden when the ruler rule is missing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new prom-rule abilities gate Pause, Restore, ModifyExport and DeletePermanently on `isAlertingRule`, while the ruler version used `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule`, which is true for Grafana recording rules too. WHY: Grafana-managed recording rules in the list view no longer offer Pause or Export, even though they are supported. HOW: Use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` for these entries and keep `isAlertingRule` only for Silence.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `key={key}` prop was dropped when GrafanaRuleLoader was replaced with GrafanaRuleListItem inside `rules.map`. WHY: React falls back to index keys, so items reuse the wrong component state (e.g. an open menu or the silence/delete modal) as filtered results stream in or reorder, and it logs key warnings. HOW: Restore `key={key}` on GrafanaRuleListItem.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: List items now pass only `promRule` to RuleActionsButtons, but AlertRuleMenu still shows Pause and Delete only when `rulerRule` is present (`rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` / `canDelete && rulerRule`). WHY: Pause and Delete disappear from every Grafana rule in the list view, even for users with folder edit/delete permissions, which is a functional regression from the previous ruler-backed list. HOW: Let MenuItemPauseRule and the delete handler work from the GrafanaPromRuleDTO (uid + groupIdentifier), or fetch the ruler rule when the user triggers the action.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The fourth null check validates `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`, even though its message says 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'. WHY: An AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId is accepted, and encodeTokenId then quietly builds a token id ending in ':null' instead of failing fast. HOW: Check `rawTokenId` in that call.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The matcher returns false when the grant shortcut equals the expected one, so the condition is inverted. WHY: Tokens with the correct grant are rejected and tokens with any other grant are accepted, so the assertion validates the opposite of what it intends. HOW: Negate the comparison so it returns false when the shortcut does not match.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The matcher reads the grant shortcut with substring(3, 5), but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider puts it at characters 4-6 (sessionType 0-2, tokenType 2-4, grant 4-6). WHY: The matcher compares a slice that straddles the token type and the grant (e.g. 'ta' for 'onrtac'), so it never actually checks the grant type. HOW: Use substring(4, 6).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method on the provider-facing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface, with no default implementation. WHY: Existing custom grant type factories no longer compile, or throw AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls gtf.getShortcut(), which stops the server from starting. HOW: Add a default implementation that derives a fallback shortcut, or make the encoder handle factories that do not supply one.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The reader thread is started but never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs. WHY: A read request still in flight when `deletedAll` is set can record its exception after the assertion has already passed, so the regression this test is meant to catch can go undetected and the test is flaky. HOW: Keep a reference to the Thread and call `join()` after `deletedAll.set(true)` and before the assertion.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `deletedAll.set(true)` only runs if every `remove()` call succeeds, because it is not in a finally block. WHY: If any delete throws, the non-daemon reader thread loops forever calling the groups endpoint, which leaks into the following tests and can keep the test JVM from exiting. HOW: Wrap the delete loop in try/finally and set `deletedAll` in the finally block.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The admin-ui message now uses Java MessageFormat placeholders ('{0}' and '{2,choice,...}'), but this file is consumed by i18next, which every sibling error-* key reflects with '{{0}}' syntax. WHY: The admin console will show the literal text 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' instead of the interpolated values. HOW: Keep i18next interpolation syntax and use i18next plurals or neutral wording.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The account-ui message was changed from i18next '{{0}}' interpolation to MessageFormat '{0}' with a '{2,choice,...}' construct, which i18next does not support. WHY: The account console will render the raw placeholders and choice pattern to end users instead of the attribute name and limits. HOW: Restore the '{{n}}' interpolation syntax used by this React UI.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 was replaced with an Italian sentence ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'). WHY: Lithuanian users see Italian text on the OTP setup login page. HOW: Use a Lithuanian translation such as 'Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:'.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The Lithuanian account totpStep1 was replaced with an Italian sentence. WHY: Lithuanian users see Italian text in the account console OTP setup. HOW: Replace it with a Lithuanian translation of 'Install one of the following applications on your mobile:'.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) totpStep1 was replaced with Traditional Chinese text ('手機', '應用程式'). WHY: zh_CN users see mixed Traditional characters that don't match the rest of the locale. HOW: Use the Simplified form '在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：'.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent:
WHAT: The common prefix (start) and suffix (end) are computed independently, so start + end can exceed the shorter string's length. For example, value '>
' vs sanitized '>' gives start=1 and end=1, and sanitized.substring(1, 0) is called. WHY: This throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and crashes the Maven plugin instead of reporting the illegal HTML. HOW: Limit the suffix loop with `end < Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: If the derived English counterpart of a messages_*.properties file doesn't exist, verifySafeHtml throws a RuntimeException instead of adding a validation message. WHY: The ThemeVerifierMojo applies to every messages_* file in the project's resources, so a single locale file without an _en sibling crashes the build with an unhandled exception. HOW: On FileNotFoundException, add an entry to `messages` (or fall back to an empty English bundle) and return.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: getClientsWithPermission looks up resources of type "Clients", but getOrCreateResource creates per-client V2 resources without a type. The only match is the type-level resource, so the method returns {"Clients"} instead of client IDs. WHY: AvailableRoleMappingResource:230 calls realm.getClientById("Clients").getRolesStream(), which throws a NullPointerException, and permissions granted on individual clients are never returned. HOW: Iterate the per-client resources (for example, find the policies attached to Clients-scope resources and resolve their resource names), and handle the type-level resource separately so it is never returned as a client ID.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: setPermissionsEnabled now throws UnsupportedOperationException, but the ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions:91 still calls it whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever V2 is enabled. WHY: when both features are enabled, deleting any client throws inside the removal event and the deletion fails; before this PR the inherited V1 implementation handled the call. HOW: Make setPermissionsEnabled a no-op in V2, or skip the V1 cleanup in the listener when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: canExchangeTo now throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider:276 still calls AdminPermissions.management(...).clients().canExchangeTo(...), and that returns ClientPermissionsV2 whenever V2 is enabled. WHY: token exchange to a target client now fails with a server error instead of an allow/deny decision when V2 and token exchange are enabled together. HOW: Return false (deny) instead of throwing, or keep the inherited V1 behavior until V2 supports token exchange.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: configuredFor now returns true for users who only have a passkey, but only keycloak.v2/login/login-password.ftl got the passkeys macro; base/login/login-password.ftl has no webauthn form or button. WHY: In base-derived themes ("keycloak" and custom themes), a passkey-only user reaching a required PasswordForm sees a password field they cannot use and no passkey option, and the old not-configured path (setting the password required action) is skipped. HOW: Add `<@passkeys.conditionalUIData />` (and its import) to base/login/login-password.ftl so every theme that inherits it shows the passkey option.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate checks the login predicate against `idpById`, which comes from getById() and is wrapped by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so isEnabled() returns false whenever the linked organization is disabled. WHY: if an org-linked public IdP is set to hideOnLogin/linkOnly while its org is disabled, both checks fail, the login caches are not invalidated, and once the org is re-enabled the cached id is returned and the login page shows a hidden/link-only IdP (the bean only re-checks isEnabled). HOW: run the predicate against the unwrapped stored model (e.g. idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId())) instead of the org-aware wrapper.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The cleanup is registered for an IdP with the literal alias "alias" instead of the alias actually created ("idp-alias-" + i). WHY: none of the 21 IdPs created in testCacheIDPForLogin are removed, so state leaks into later tests in the realm. HOW: capture the real alias for the cleanup.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC condition to the shared getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, which the base (non-organization) login bean uses to filter the user's already-linked IdPs. WHY: when the organization feature is disabled, a user whose linked IdP still has an organizationId but is not public no longer sees that IdP on the login page, a regression unrelated to caching. HOW: keep the org condition in a separate predicate used only for cache invalidation in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Every distinct organizationId passed to getForLogin calls invalidateObject on the single per-realm/per-mode cache entry and re-adds it with all previously cached org id sets merged in. WHY: in realms with many organizations the login path triggers repeated cluster-wide invalidations, and one ever-growing cache entry is rebuilt on each new org lookup. HOW: include the organizationId in the cache key (one entry per org) instead of merging search keys into one entry.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids).values() using zip, assuming the returned dict keeps input order and has the same length. WHY: get_multi removes duplicate ids and merges cached items after the service results (items.update(cache_items)), so the order and length can differ and errors end up with the wrong id or are silently dropped. HOW: look up each event by its node id instead of zipping.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: gen_request_data compares error timestamps in seconds (from nodestore event data) with rrweb event timestamps, which are millisecond integers (event_parser types the top-level timestamp as int ms). WHY: every error timestamp is numerically smaller than every breadcrumb timestamp, so all errors are emitted before the first breadcrumb and the timeline sent to Seer is not in chronological order. HOW: normalize to one unit before comparing, e.g. compare error['timestamp'] * 1000 with event['timestamp'].

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Every paginated GET now runs query_replay_instance and then a nodestore get_multi over all of the replay's error_ids, with no cap and before pagination. WHY: a replay with many errors loads every full event payload from nodestore on every page request, which adds large latency and memory use to a request that already calls Seer. HOW: cap error_ids (e.g. error_ids[:N]) before calling fetch_error_details.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: validate_timestamp and validate_age check whether the other field is truthy, so age=0 (or timestamp=0) is treated as absent. WHY: a report with both timestamp and age=0 passes validation, which defeats the stated rule that the two fields are mutually exclusive. HOW: check for key presence with `"age" in self.initial_data` and `"timestamp" in self.initial_data`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The flusher processes are SpawnProcess instances (from get_context('spawn').Process), and SpawnProcess subclasses BaseProcess rather than multiprocessing.Process, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False and kill() is never called. WHY: When a process is restarted because it hung, the old process keeps running next to the new one for the same shards, which leaks processes and causes concurrent duplicate flushing; the old code always called kill(). HOW: Check against BaseProcess, or call kill() whenever the object has that method.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Each per-process SpansBuffer.get_memory_info() calls iter_cluster_memory_usage on the same cluster-wide Redis client, so submit queries memory on every cluster node once per flusher process. WHY: Every submit now sends N times as many INFO requests across the cluster, and the totals are just duplicated (the ratio does not change). HOW: Query memory info once, through any single buffer.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When the join deadline runs out, the loop `break`s, and terminate() is never called on the processes it has not visited yet. WHY: Those flusher processes can keep running after join returns and may keep flushing shards that have already been reassigned during a rebalance. HOW: Instead of breaking, skip the wait but still terminate each remaining process.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op, so the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` does not wait at all. WHY: The flusher threads still race against step.join(), which sets stopped, so `(msg,) = messages` can fail intermittently. HOW: Poll until messages is non-empty (with a bounded loop) before calling join.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the class is defined, so every AssignmentSource shares the module import timestamp. WHY: the `queued` value carried through the task kwargs is wrong for every assignment after process start, and nothing that uses this field to order or expire stale sync events can trust it. HOW: use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The OAuth `state` is `pipeline.signature`, which is a static md5 of the pipeline view class names (pipeline/base.py:132-133), so every user and session gets the same value. WHY: An attacker can make a victim with an active install pipeline open `/extensions/github/setup/?code=<attacker_code>&state=9cae5e88...`; the check passes and binds the attacker's GitHub login as `github_authenticated_user`, so the new user check does nothing against CSRF. HOW: Generate a random per-pipeline nonce (e.g. `secrets.token_hex`), store it with `pipeline.bind_state('oauth_state', ...)`, send it as `state` and compare it with `constant_time_compare`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes `sender` is always present, but build_integration only sets it when `state.get("sender")` is truthy, and installation.py:44 already handles it being missing. WHY: Reinstalling an existing Integration that has no `sender` in its metadata (for example one created through the pipeline instead of the webhook) raises KeyError and returns a 500. HOW: Read it with `.get` and treat a missing sender as a verification failure.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When no Integration row exists yet for `installation_id`, the view goes straight to `pipeline.next_step()` without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to the user who installed the app. WHY: A user can supply an `installation_id` whose installation webhook has not been processed yet, and build_integration will then link that GitHub installation to their Sentry org without checking who they are. HOW: Before continuing in the DoesNotExist branch, fetch the installation's sender/account from GitHub and compare it to `github_authenticated_user`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `get_user_info` calls `resp.raise_for_status()` and is not wrapped in error handling, and neither is `safe_urlopen`; only `safe_urlread` is inside the try/except. WHY: A rejected token or a GitHub API or network error during installation becomes a 500 instead of the `error()` page the popup expects, so the install dialog never gets its postMessage. HOW: Wrap the token exchange and the `get_user_info` call in try/except and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` when they fail.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty body, so it does not implement the abstract counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values or build_occurrence_and_event_data. WHY: Detector.detector_handler calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so every metric_alert_fire detector raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` inside process_detectors; before this PR the handler was concrete and returned no results. HOW: Implement the abstract members, or keep MetricAlertDetectorHandler on DetectorHandler with a stub evaluate returning {} until the stateful implementation is ready.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence with group_key "val1", but it evaluates group_key "group_key", so the expected and actual fingerprints differ (`<id>:val1` vs `<id>:group_key`). WHY: IssueOccurrence is a frozen dataclass that compares fingerprint in __eq__, so `evaluate_group_key_value(...) == expected_result` fails. HOW: Pass "group_key" to build_mock_occurrence_and_event.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: get_monitor_environment_context builds `config` with a readable schedule_type, but the return value uses the raw `monitor_environment.monitor.config`, so that copy is never used. WHY: the monitor context sent with each occurrence contains the numeric schedule_type instead of its display value. HOW: return `config` instead of `monitor_environment.monitor.config`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside it, checkIfIsAvailable returns true right away and never runs the busy check. WHY: Existing bookings and calendar busy times are ignored on override days, so already-booked slots are offered and can be double-booked. HOW: Remove the early return so the busy.every check still runs; use dateOverrideExist only to skip the working-hours check.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Two different Dayjs instances are compared with ===, which is reference equality and always false. WHY: A day-off override (start equals end) is never detected, so a slot starting exactly at the override time passes the later range checks and stays bookable. HOW: Use `.isSame()` to compare the two times.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The end-bound check uses slotStartTime.isAfter(override end) instead of checking the slot's end time. WHY: A slot that starts inside the override but runs past its end (e.g. a 60-minute slot at 10:30 for a 10:00-11:00 override) is accepted, so a host can be booked outside their override hours. HOW: Reject the slot when slotEndTime is after the override end.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The start-bound check only rejects slots that end at or before the override start; it never checks whether the slot starts before the override. WHY: A slot that begins before the override window and ends inside it is treated as available, so fixed hosts can be booked partly outside their override hours. HOW: Reject the slot when slotStartTime is before the override start.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `end` is computed from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so it always equals `start`. WHY: Slots that start inside working hours but end after them (e.g. a 60-minute slot at 16:30 when work ends at 17:00) are not rejected. HOW: Compute `end` from slotEndTime.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The working-hours check marks a slot unavailable if ANY working-hours range on that weekday does not contain it. WHY: Users with split availability (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17 on the same day) have every slot rejected, because each slot falls outside at least one range, so no slots are offered at all. HOW: Mark the slot unavailable only when no range for that day contains it (use some/every over the ranges for that day).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The override date is formatted with `dayjs(...)`, which uses the server's local timezone, while the slot date is formatted in UTC. WHY: On a server not running in UTC, the day comparison is off for overrides near midnight, so overrides get applied to the wrong day or skipped. HOW: Use dayjs.utc(date.start) before adding the offset and formatting.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: After the timezone offset is added, startTime/endTime are computed as hour*60+minute, which wraps at midnight. WHY: For overrides that cross the invitee's midnight (e.g. 20:00-23:00 UTC shown to a +6:00 invitee), endTime ends up smaller than startTime, so buildSlots produces no slots or slots in the wrong part of the day. HOW: Compute minutes relative to the start of the invitee's day (e.g. diff in minutes from startOfInviteeDay) instead of taking hour/minute of the shifted time.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Each `import()` in the appStore object literal runs as soon as the module loads, so all 28 app packages are fetched and evaluated immediately, and each one creates a promise with no rejection handler until some caller happens to await that key. WHY: Nothing is lazily loaded, so cold-start cost is unchanged. If any app module fails to load (missing env-dependent dependency, top-level throw), Node reports an unhandled rejection, which can crash the process even when that app is never used. HOW: Store loader functions (`applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and call them at lookup sites (`await appStore[key]?.()`).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The forEach callback is now async and awaits getCalendar, so getCalendar errors and deleteEvent errors become rejected promises that forEach drops. WHY: Before, a synchronous getCalendar throw failed the requestReschedule mutation. Now it surfaces as an unhandled rejection after the response, and calendar deletions run detached and are never awaited. HOW: Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => {...}))`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Turning the forEach callback async moves the awaited getCalendar call out of the surrounding try/catch, because forEach discards the promise the callback returns. WHY: getCalendar failures that `logger.error` used to catch now become unhandled promise rejections, and the deletes are never awaited. The same change exists in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts. HOW: Replace the forEach with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => {...}))` inside the try.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The reminder cancel/delete calls inside forEach are now fire-and-forget async calls. The old code awaited the prisma deletes through prismaPromises. WHY: The handler can respond before the reminder rows are flagged `cancelled` or deleted, and in a serverless runtime that work can be dropped, so the reminders of a cancelled booking still go out. HOW: Collect the promises returned by deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder and add them to the Promise.all that is already awaited.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: requestReschedule no longer awaits reminder cancellation (`await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` was removed), and the async delete helpers are called without await inside forEach. WHY: The mutation can finish before the old booking's reminders are flagged `cancelled` or deleted, so reminders for the rescheduled booking can still be sent. HOW: Map the reminders to the returned promises and `await Promise.all(...)` them.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: All SendGrid cancel requests run inside one try, so the first failing `client.request` throws out of the loop and `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` never runs. WHY: No cancelled reminder is deleted in that run, and the same failing reminder comes back on every later run, so the reminders after it are never cancelled and those emails are sent. HOW: Put the try/catch around each reminder so one failure does not block the rest.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The reschedule path calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true. That sends the SendGrid cancel right away and does not flag or delete the reminder row. WHY: The PR says immediate SendGrid cancels are what stopped working because cancelled batches accumulate. Rescheduling is a frequent path, so it keeps filling that list, while requestReschedule uses the deferred `cancelled` flag for the same case. HOW: Drop the `true` argument so the reminder is flagged `cancelled` and the cron cancels it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object `{}`, and Prisma does not write @updatedAt when no field is being updated. WHY: SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is never bumped after the cache refresh, so the intended 'last refreshed' signal for this credential's calendars never changes. HOW: Pass an explicit timestamp, e.g. `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: After a successful cache delete, the component does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. It only calls the optional `onSuccess` prop, which SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper forwards from an optional `props.onChanged`. WHY: When the parent does not pass onChanged, the dropdown keeps showing the old 'Last updated' timestamp and the delete option for cache that is already gone, until the page reloads. HOW: Add `onSettled` to invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, as the disconnect mutation already does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When the credential is missing or not owned, the handler throws a plain `Error` instead of a `TRPCError`. WHY: tRPC maps it to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500), so an expected authorization or not-found case shows up as a server failure and is logged as one. HOW: Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", message: ... })`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `sed -i '' -E ...` uses BSD/macOS in-place syntax. WHY: On GNU sed (Linux), `''` is read as the sed script and the real expression as a filename, so the command fails and GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated when the key already exists. HOW: Use a portable form such as `sed -i.bak -E "..." "$ENV_FILE" && rm -f "$ENV_FILE.bak"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count and saves, but UsersController#create runs validations twice (user.valid? at line 168, then user.save at line 172). WHY: every blocked signup attempt is counted twice, so the match_count stats this PR adds are wrong. HOW: don't write to the database from inside validation. Have the validator call a side-effect-free check and record the match once, e.g. after save fails or only on the save path.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: should_block? matches the email with an exact, case-sensitive where(email: email), and User does not normalize the email's case before validating. WHY: a blocked address can still sign up by changing its case (e.g. 'Bad@Spammers.org' when 'bad@spammers.org' is blocked). HOW: downcase emails when storing BlockedEmail records and when looking them up, e.g. where('lower(email) = ?', email.to_s.downcase).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: match_count is incremented as read, +1 in Ruby, then save, which is not atomic. WHY: when signup attempts for the same email run at the same time, both read the same value and one increment is lost. HOW: do an atomic SQL update, e.g. BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now]).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil, or a row whose `notification_level` is NULL, and the code then calls `tu.notification_level >` without a guard. WHY: A user with no topic_users row for the topic, or with a NULL level (the `tracking` scope's COALESCE shows NULL is valid), gets a NoMethodError/500 instead of being unsubscribed. HOW: Read the current level with a fallback to regular and write it through `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row if needed.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Each GET of the unsubscribe URL lowers the level one more step (watching/tracking to regular, then regular to muted), so the action is not idempotent. WHY: A reload, a browser prefetch, or a mail security scanner fetching the link before the user clicks it ends up muting the topic, which the user did not ask for. HOW: Always set one fixed target level, for example muted or regular, instead of stepping down from whatever the current level is.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `topics#unsubscribe` is routed as GET but changes the current user's notification_level, and it is not protected by a CSRF token. WHY: Any external page or email can embed `` and silently lower or mute notifications on any topic for a logged-in victim. HOW: Require a per-user signed token in the email link, or have the GET page confirm and do the change through a CSRF-protected PUT/POST.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The client route's model hook only loads the topic view JSON and never calls the server `unsubscribe` action. WHY: If the user reaches /t/slug/id/unsubscribe by in-app navigation instead of a full page load, the page says notifications will stop, but nothing changes on the server.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The light-theme argument was changed from `$lightness: 30%` to `70%`, and the dark argument was flipped to `$secondary 30%`. WHY: Because dark-light-choose returns its first argument for light themes, the bold reply-to link in topic-meta-data h5 is now much lighter and low-contrast in the default theme, and on dark themes it gets the wrong shade too. HOW: Keep the original value: light 30%, dark 70%.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `.custom-message-length` now uses `$primary 30%` for light themes and `$secondary 70%` for dark themes, the reverse of the original 70% and of the desktop version. WHY: On mobile light themes the hint text becomes much darker than before, and dark themes get the wrong shade. HOW: Use `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`, matching desktop/modal.scss.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The light-theme color for the topic-map `h3` was changed from `$lightness: 20%` to `50%`. WHY: Mobile light themes get noticeably lighter headings, which is a visual regression this PR was not meant to cause; desktop/topic-post.scss:321 keeps 20%/80%. HOW: Use `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `.name` color was changed from `$lightness: 30%` to `50%` in the light-theme branch. WHY: The light theme now shows the name at the same dimmer shade as `.title`, so the two no longer contrast. HOW: Use `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `.name` color was changed from `$lightness: 30%` to `50%` in the light-theme branch. WHY: Mobile light themes render the user name lighter than before, so it can no longer be told apart from `.title`. HOW: Use `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `website_name` is added as a plain attribute but not to `untrusted_attributes`, so the `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` check that hides `website` for TL0 users seen by anonymous visitors never runs for it. WHY: anonymous visitors get the TL0 user's website host and path through `website_name`, and user.hbs renders it, which defeats the anti-spam hiding of new users' websites. HOW: add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (and delete the custom include method) so it is gated exactly like `website`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `include_website_name` has no trailing `?`, so ActiveModel::Serializers, which looks for `include_<attr>?`, never calls it. WHY: the intended condition is dead code and `website_name` is always serialized, as nil when the user has no website. HOW: rename it to `include_website_name?`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Targets are now run through applyTemplateVariables (with request.filters) before splitting, and they go through it again later. Each split sub-request (`{ ...request, targets }`) is sent through datasource.runQuery -> DataSourceWithBackend.query, which calls applyTemplateVariables again with the same scopedVars and filters (DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185). WHY: addFilterAsLabelFilter (modifyQuery.ts:511) does not check for duplicates, so ad hoc filters on parsed or structured-metadata labels are added twice (e.g. `{app="x"} | json | level=`info` | level=`info``), and variable values containing `$` are expanded a second time. The non-split path interpolates only once, so the two paths now send different queries. HOW: Clear the ad hoc filters on the sub-requests (e.g. build them with `filters: undefined`) or skip the second interpolation, so each query is interpolated exactly once.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: runShardSplitQuery now applies applyTemplateVariables(query, scopedVars, request.filters) up front, but the sharded sub-requests keep request.filters/scopedVars. datasource.runQuery -> DataSourceWithBackend.query then calls applyTemplateVariables on them again. WHY: Ad hoc filters on non-indexed labels are appended twice by addFilterAsLabelFilter, which does not check for duplicates, and `$` sequences inside already-interpolated values are re-expanded, so sharded queries differ from what the user built. HOW: Remove `filters` from the sub-requests passed to runQuery, or make sure the backend-layer interpolation is not applied a second time.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: enableSqlExpressions assigns `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` and returns false on both branches, so the flag lookup is dead code and the variable name means the opposite of its value. WHY: the code looks like a flag gate but ignores the flag; if someone changes the final `return false` to restore flag behavior, the inverted `enabled` makes the flag work backwards. HOW: make the kill switch explicit with a single `return false` and a comment, and drop the misleading flag lookup.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The denial cache is checked before any permission source and is never invalidated when permissions change or a resource is created. WHY: If a Check on a UID runs before the dashboard/folder is created or before access is granted, the user keeps getting `Allowed:false` for the whole shortCacheTTL, even though the new permCache-miss database fallback would now allow it. That is the stale-deny behaviour this PR is meant to fix. HOW: Don't short-circuit on the denial entry when the database has never confirmed the resource exists. Or, simpler, drop the denial-cache short-circuit and rely on the refetch path, possibly with a much shorter TTL for denials.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When the cached permission map exists but does not allow the resource, Check now ignores it and calls getIdentityPermissions, which always runs permissionStore.GetUserPermissions against the database. WHY: Each distinct denied resource (per user and action, per TTL window) now costs a full permission query, where before it cost none. Per-item checks over search/list results the user cannot access therefore cause O(N) database queries, and singleflight only merges concurrent calls with the same key. HOW: Refetch at most once per user+action within a short window, for example with a 'recently refreshed' marker on userPermCacheKey, instead of once per denied resource.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: userPermDenialCacheKey joins name and parent with '_', and resource UIDs can contain '_', so different (name, parent) pairs produce the same key (e.g. name='a_b',parent='' and name='a',parent='b_'). WHY: A cached denial for one resource is returned for a different resource, wrongly denying access for the TTL. HOW: Use a separator that cannot appear in UIDs, or length-prefix or encode each component.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: newRemoteRBACClient still wraps the remote authz client in a 30s authzlib LocalCache, while only the in-proc client was switched to NoopCache. WHY: In standalone/remote deployments, Check and List results are still served from the client cache. Newly created dashboards and folders and fresh grants stay invisible for up to 30s, so the server-side refetch logic never runs. HOW: Use NoopCache for the remote client too, or a cache that does not store denied results.

suggestions.label: bug
