suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Debug log calls fire at Error level on every cleanup batch, including successful ones, and print the full list of IDs (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize entries). WHY: Normal cleanup runs flood the logs with fake errors and huge payloads, which can set off error-based alerts and hide real failures. HOW: Remove these calls, or switch them to r.log.Debug and log only the counts.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The cleanup ticker interval went from 10 minutes to 1 minute, but clean() still uses a 9-minute timeout sized for the 10-minute interval. WHY: Every cleanup job (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations) now runs 10x more often against the DB, and runs back-to-back whenever a pass takes more than a minute. This looks like a debugging change left in. HOW: Restore the 10-minute interval.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: On every database except SQLite, deleteByIDs binds one placeholder per ID, so the parameter count equals AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize. WHY: MySQL and Postgres cap a statement at 65535 placeholders, so a batch size above that now fails every cleanup run; the old subquery version had no bind parameters and worked. HOW: Split ids into chunks under the driver limit before building placeholders, or inline the int64 values for every dialect.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The SQLite inline IN list is built by calling fmt.Sprintf on the growing string once per ID. That is O(n²) copying and allocation in the batch size. WHY: At batch sizes like the 32767 used in the new test, each batch copies gigabytes of string data, which slows cleanup and puts heavy pressure on the GC. HOW: Build the list with strings.Builder and strconv.AppendInt.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The fail-fast exception for multiple crypto providers was replaced by sorting on order(), but DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider and WildFlyElytronProvider all return 200. A tie between them is now settled by ServiceLoader discovery order, and the loser is only logged at debug level. WHY: A FIPS deployment that accidentally also has the default (non-FIPS BouncyCastle) provider on the classpath used to fail at startup; now it can silently run with the non-FIPS provider. HOW: Keep throwing IllegalStateException when the two highest-ordered providers have the same order() value.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The test creates one EC key pair with the default KeyPairGenerator settings (a 256-bit curve) and uses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512. WHY: The ES384 and ES512 cases never produce 48- or 66-byte r/s values or a DER sequence longer than 127 bytes, so the long-form length branches in ASN1Encoder.writeLength and ASN1Decoder.readLength are never tested and a bug there would go unnoticed. HOW: Generate a key pair on the matching curve (secp256r1, secp384r1, secp521r1) for each algorithm.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `int order()` is added to the public CryptoProvider SPI as an abstract method with no default. WHY: Any CryptoProvider implementation outside this repository stops compiling, and an already compiled one fails with AbstractMethodError when detectProvider calls CryptoProvider::order. HOW: Declare it as a default method that returns a base value, for example `default int order() { return 0; }`.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: canManage() returns true when the caller has only the VIEW scope on all groups, because it passes AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW to hasPermission. WHY: GroupsResource (line 181) uses auth.groups().requireManage() to guard top-level group creation, so an admin granted only all-groups VIEW can create groups (privilege escalation). HOW: check only the MANAGE scope.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission looks up and returns groupResource.getId() (the internal resource id), but group resources are named by group id (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup) and hasPermission resolves them with findByName. WHY: the lookup always misses and falls back to the all-groups resource, and the returned set holds resource ids. JpaUserProvider then uses that set as a group-id filter, so user search and count return the wrong users, or none. HOW: pass and collect groupResource.getName(), as ClientPermissionsV2 does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: canView(GroupModel) does not check canView() (the all-groups VIEW/MANAGE permission), and GroupsResource/GroupResource no longer short-circuit with canViewGlobal. When a group has its own resource, hasPermission evaluates only that resource. WHY: an admin with an all-groups VIEW permission is denied view (and the group is filtered out of listings) for any group that has a specific permission resource without the VIEW scope. HOW: return true early when canView() is true, as V1 does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The PR renumbers the exit codes (RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE 4→3, and 4 is reused for FEATURE_DISABLED), but testFeatureNotEnabled and testWrongVersions only check messages, not exit codes. WHY: The exit code is the documented contract for automation scripts, so a wrong or swapped value (for example, feature-disabled reported as recreate) would pass the suite. HOW: Assert `assertEquals(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED, cliResult.exitCode())` in testFeatureNotEnabled and `assertEquals(CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE, result.exitCode())` after each incompatible check in testWrongVersions.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: getCredential always calls getFederatedCredentialsStream first. For LDAP-federated users this runs LDAPStorageProvider.getCredentials, which queries LDAP and throws IllegalStateException when the LDAP object is not found. WHY: recovery-code login and the RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean page now fail with a 500 (and pay an LDAP round-trip on every call) for federated users whose recovery codes are stored locally, where before only local storage was read. HOW: check local stored credentials first and only fall back to the federated stream, or only consult the federated provider when it supports the recovery-codes type.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: when user storage accepts the new recovery codes, the local `createCredential` is skipped, and that call is the only place an existing local recovery-codes credential gets deleted. WHY: UserCredentialManager.isValid still runs the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider, so codes the user meant to replace by regenerating still authenticate. HOW: when userStorageCreated is true, remove any existing local recovery-codes credential.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the user-storage path serializes the raw plaintext recovery codes (`generatedCodes`) into the UserCredentialModel, while the local path stores only the hashed codes from credentialModel. WHY: any user storage provider receives and may persist plaintext recovery codes, so a leak of the external store exposes working second-factor codes. HOW: pass the hashed credential data (credentialModel.getCredentialData()) to the user storage instead of the raw codes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the credential can now come from user storage, but when all codes are used it is still deleted with `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`, which only acts on the local store. WHY: a federated credential (whose id may be null when built via createFromValues) is never removed from the user storage, so the exhausted credential stays configured. HOW: when the credential has a federation link or came from the federated stream, remove it through the storage provider (e.g. disableCredentialType) instead of removeStoredCredentialById.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), but the audit log endpoint uses it with order_by='-datetime', so the value is a datetime. WHY: build_cursor calls this key on the result rows and math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError, so every non-empty optimized_pagination request returns a 500. HOW: Convert datetimes to epoch milliseconds, as DateTimePaginator.get_item_key does, or subclass DateTimePaginator.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value, and build_queryset puts it directly into a `datetime <= %s` filter for the '-datetime' key. WHY: Comparing an integer millisecond timestamp to a datetime column either fails in the database or filters the wrong rows, so following any next/prev cursor is broken. HOW: Convert the cursor value back to a UTC datetime, as DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When enable_advanced_features is set, a client-supplied negative cursor offset is passed straight to queryset[start_offset:stop]. WHY: Django QuerySets reject negative indexing with ValueError/AssertionError, and paginate() only catches BadPaginationError, so a cursor like `0:-5:0` gives an unhandled 500. HOW: Reject negative offsets by raising BadPaginationError, or clamp them to 0.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: enable_advanced dereferences organization_context.member.has_global_access on every request, and member can be None for non-superuser principals that pass OrganizationAuditPermission without an org membership. WHY: Because the line runs before the use_optimized check, those requests now raise AttributeError and return a 500 even when the default paginator would have been used. HOW: Check use_optimized first and guard against a missing member.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: _is_error_focused_query uses a plain substring check, so a query like '!event.type:error' or 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction' is treated as errors-only. WHY: for allowlisted projects on the discover dataset, count() is rewritten to upsampled_count() for queries that exclude errors or include transactions, and the returned counts are wrong. HOW: parse the query with the event search parser and only return True when there is one positive, non-negated event.type:error filter with no OR branches.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: count() is rewritten to 'upsampled_count() as count', which always produces a result column named 'count'. With transformAliasToInputFormat=1, the serializer instead looks for the column 'count()', because resolve_axis_column uses the original query_columns in organization_events.py. WHY: for allowlisted error queries that use transformAliasToInputFormat, the series lookup misses and the endpoint returns empty or zero-filled data instead of the upsampled counts. HOW: make the alias of the rewritten column match whatever resolve_axis_column will look up, for example alias it to the original column name when transform_alias_to_input_format is enabled.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Every strategy built by create_thread_queue_parallel_worker reuses the single factory-level self.queue_pool, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/join()/terminate() call queue_pool.shutdown() on that shared pool. WHY: After the first partition rebalance, the next strategy submits into shut-down queues. queue.put raises ShutDown, the except in submit() marks the offset complete, and messages are committed without ever being processed. HOW: Create a new FixedQueuePool per create_with_partitions call, or stop shutting down the shared pool in close() and only shut it down in factory.shutdown().

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: _commit_loop calls the arroyo Commit callback from a background daemon thread instead of from the strategy's submit/poll on the main thread. WHY: arroyo's commit changes StreamProcessor state and commits offsets on the KafkaConsumer, which is not thread-safe, while the main thread is polling the same consumer at the same time. This can cause races, lost commits, or commits landing during a rebalance. HOW: Have the background thread (or poll()) compute committable offsets, then call self.commit_function inside poll() on the main thread.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Work queues are created as unbounded queue.Queue(), and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit never raises MessageRejected, so arroyo gets no backpressure. WHY: When processing falls behind (the slow-item case this PR targets), the consumer keeps pulling messages and buffering full Message objects in memory without limit, which can exhaust memory and cause a huge redelivery after a crash. HOW: Give each queue a maxsize and, in submit, use put_nowait and raise MessageRejected on queue.Full so arroyo retries the message.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: get_committable_offsets stops advancing at the first offset in range(start, max+1) that was never added to all_offsets. WHY: Kafka offsets can be non-contiguous (transaction control markers, compacted topics), so a single offset that is never delivered stops commits for that partition forever while all_offsets keeps growing. HOW: Walk the sorted list of seen offsets above last_committed and stop only at the first one that is still outstanding, instead of requiring every integer to be present.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True before calling q.shutdown(immediate=False), so each worker exits its while loop after its current item instead of draining the queue. WHY: Items still in the queues are dropped at shutdown, which defeats the graceful drain that immediate=False is meant to provide and forces reprocessing on restart. HOW: Do not set worker.shutdown; let workers drain until get() raises queue.ShutDown.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The script now runs ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE on segment keys that consumers on the previous version created with SADD as plain sets, and those keys live for up to redis_ttl (3600s). WHY: During a rolling deploy, or for up to an hour after it, Redis returns WRONGTYPE for these keys, so the EVALSHA fails and p.execute() in process_spans raises, crashing the consumer batch. HOW: Use a new key prefix for the sorted-set buffers (e.g. `span-buf:z:`) so old and new data never collide, or check the key with TYPE and migrate or skip legacy sets.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: ZUNIONSTORE is called without AGGREGATE, so it defaults to SUM and adds the scores of a payload that appears in both sets. WHY: A duplicate span (e.g. a Kafka redelivery) ends up with a score of about twice its end timestamp, so ZPOPMIN never evicts it and the eviction no longer follows end time. HOW: Pass `AGGREGATE MAX` (or MIN) so a duplicate member keeps its real timestamp.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The max_segment_spans check was removed from _load_segment_data and the limit is now hardcoded as 1000 in add-buffer.lua, so the SpansBuffer `max_segment_spans` parameter (default 1001) is never read. WHY: Any caller or config that sets max_segment_spans is silently ignored, and the effective limit (1000) also differs from the documented default.
